heading: Sravanabelagola, Mysore · Ganga period, c. 980 CE

items.label: Temple / Image
items.title: The Gommata image on Indragiri
items.alt: Hypothetical reconstruction of the colossal Gommata image erected at Sravanabelagola under Ganga patronage.
items.attested: Epigraphia Carnatica vol. II, Rice 1889, Sravanabelagola inscriptions (nos. 75-77 for the Gommata image: Chavundaraya, minister of the Ganga king Racha-malla/Marasimha) with Rice's introduction on Gomata/Gommata (pp. 23-24 of the OCR) on the colossal standing image, its location and descriptive details as given by Rice.
items.prescribed: Rice's own description of the surviving image (creepers twining the legs and arms, half-smile) is a late scholarly secondary source; the surviving monument is a check.
items.conjecture: The 1116 cloisters (Hoysala era) are excluded. Anything not in the epigraphs: surrounding structures at c. 980, pilgrims, dress. This is a surviving monument, not a described temple building. The image shows the statue in the traditional Digambara Jain convention of an unclothed standing saint; the surrounding hill, pilgrims and their dress are the painter's.
items.note: Hypothetical reconstruction painted with an AI image model from Epigraphia Carnatica II (Rice 1889); not an archaeological finding.
